findings.claim: Replacing `util.mergeDefs` with an object spread re-introduces eager evaluation of the object def's lazy `shape` getter (and drops any non-enumerable/accessor descriptors on the def). This is exactly what the removed comment warned about, and the same regression applies to `passthrough`/`loose`/`strict`/`strip` immediately below.
findings.rationale: In Zod v4 `ZodObject`'s def `shape` is commonly installed as a lazy getter (e.g. when the shape is supplied as a thunk or participates in a recursive/self-referential schema). `{ ...this._zod.def }` invokes every enumerable getter, so calling `.catchall()`/`.strict()`/`.passthrough()` now forces the whole shape subtree to be materialized at call time — a perf regression and, for mutually recursive schemas, a possible infinite recursion/stack overflow. It also converts the getter into a snapshot value, so later resolution of the lazy shape is no longer reflected in the cloned schema. Worse, if `shape` is defined as a non-enumerable property, the spread drops it entirely and the clone ends up with `def.shape === undefined`. `mergeDefs` exists specifically to copy descriptors without triggering them; the explicit comment on the removed line strongly suggests this was a deliberate prior fix being undone. Confidence: high that this is a real behavioral regression, moderate on which failure mode (perf vs. recursion) bites first.

findings.claim: `strip()` now spreads an explicit `catchall: undefined` onto the def instead of going through `mergeDefs`, which may leave an own `catchall` key present rather than removing it.
findings.rationale: `util.mergeDefs` typically skips/deletes keys whose value is `undefined`, whereas the spread form always creates an own `catchall` property with value `undefined`. Any consumer that uses `"catchall" in def`, `Object.keys(def)`, JSON serialization of the def, or descriptor-based cloning will now see a difference (e.g. `strip()` output no longer structurally equal to a freshly constructed strip object). Most internal checks are truthiness-based so this may be benign, but it is a real shape change worth confirming. Confidence: moderate, depends on `mergeDefs`' undefined handling.
